newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader tries to settle local Coke strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader tries to settle local Coke strike.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has intervened to try to settle a 10-week-old strike at two Coca-Cola bottling plants on the island, a union leader said on Thursday.

"The president called us for a meeting yesterday to try to bring about a settlement between the management and union labour," said Bala Tampoe, leader of the Ceylon Mercantile Union, which represents the strikers. "She met the management earlier."

More than 700 workers are on strike at two bottling plants run by Pure Beverages, the island's sole local Coke bottler and a 51 percent subsidiary of F&NCC, a joint venture of Coca-Cola and Singapore's Fraser & Neave.
A Pure Beverages spokesman declined comment on the company's talks with Kumaratunga, but said an announcement might be made on Friday.
The strike, to protest against planned layoffs, has shut down Coca-Cola production in Sri Lanka since December 12.
Analysts said the strike had had no visible impact on the market as there were plenty of other soft drinks available.
Coca-Cola's daily output before the strike was 40,000 cases.
